Maria: Ran a 4h profiling sweep on prod-serving last night. Observed a ~2.7x spike in kernel switches for routes: /v1/generate-short and /v1/chat-light between 23:40-00:30 UTC. Queue wait p50/p95 moved from 8ms/24ms -> 35ms/210ms. Uploading flamegraph + histogram snapshot: https://internal.grafana/redwood/fg/1782001234

Kevin: Thanks — saw something similar on canary earlier. Batch size histogram collapsed: huge mass at size=1 for short-seq routes. Scheduler sampling seems to prefer immediate dispatch when kernel = slow_path, which increases context-switch overhead.

Maria: Repro instructions I used:
```bash
# replay synthetic load for short seqs
wrk -t8 -c200 -d600s --script=short_seq.lua http://svc.local/v1/generate-short
# capture runtime profile
curl -s http://svc.local/debug/pprof > /tmp/pprof.pb
```

Alex: Grafana panel note — token-level latency breakdown needs to be split by route + kernel_tag. Current panel aggregates across kernels which hides the handoff spikes. Suggested PromQL: `histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(token_latency_bucket[5m])) by (le, route, kernel_tag))` and add `route=~"/v1/(generate|chat)-.*"` filter for the short routes.

Sree: Quick hypothesis: KV-cache churn for short-prefix hits causing extra memcopies on cache miss, leading to scheduler forcing small batches so kernels switch more. I ran microbenchmarks: KV miss cost ~120us extra per token for seq_len<=16. If cache TTL tuned wrong we could see regression after cache eviction bursts.

Dana: We should expose queue_wait_ms percentiles per-route in the console and add a per-route KPI: `p50_queue_wait_ms`, `p95_queue_wait_ms`, `batch_efficiency` (avg_batch_size / max_possible). Also add an alert: p95_queue_wait_ms > 150ms for 2m.

Kevin: Two quick experiments I can run:
1) force kernel preference to `kernel_fast_small` for seq<=32 and measure.
2) increase min_batch_timeout from 1ms -> 5ms for affected nodes to see if batch size recovers.

Sree: Config snippet to force kernel (test-only):
```yaml
runtime_override:
  route_filter: "/v1/generate-short"
  kernel_hint: "kernel_fast_small"
  max_seq: 32
```

infra-bot: deploy:service/prod-serving@2026-03-12T00:05:12Z — rollout started (canary=5%).

Maria: Profiling summary: kernel-switch overhead + kv-miss tail are the dominant contributors to extra token tail latency. Action items:
- Kevin to run the two experiments and post microbench numbers (due EOD).
- Alex to add kernel_tag dimension & queue_wait percentiles to the token-latency dashboard (PR + panel by tomorrow).
- Sree to run KV-cache ttl/reuse tests and measure miss rate (sync in 12h).
- Dana to add alerts for p95_queue_wait_ms and batch_efficiency drop.

Kevin: Acked. Will start experiment 1 now and share a short gist with numbers.

Maria: If any of the experiments shows >10% improvement on p95 token latency, we can roll kernel_hint to canary 50% and monitor per-route KPIs before wider rollout.

Dana: Fine by me. Also recommend we capture a targeted flamegraph right at the scheduler boundary — that helped last time.

Alex: I'll queue the dashboard changes. Leaving notes for panel owners to watch model-switch counts too.

Maria: Thanks all — ping here with numbers. :rocket:
